%% W18: Section 7 read against the closed form of \ref{sec:app_setups}.
%% Anchors: the paragraph now at main.tex lines 1578-1599, and the
%% 'trajectory advantage over Boris' row of Table~\ref{tab:seeds} (line 1663).

%% --- ANCHOR A: replaces the sentence beginning 'Against a Boris reference at a step $150$ times smaller' (line 1578-1582).
Lengthening the run reverses what is left.  Against the closed form of the
problem---Bessel of order zero in the Larmor frame, \ref{sec:app_setups}---the
trajectory advantage of the corrector is $120.1$ at $19.1$ gyro-orbits, $32.8$ at
$50$, unity at $101$, and $0.067$ at $200$.  At $10^{3}$ gyro-orbits the corrector
is worse than Boris by a factor of $143$ and at $10^{4}$ by a factor of $1575$.

%% --- ANCHOR B: replaces the sentence 'Measured against the closed form, that
%% reference carries $1.396\times10^{-3}$ ... An advantage above $298$ therefore
%% reports a corrector error below the error of the ruler.' (lines 1589-1593).
The Boris reference at $h/150$ that earlier versions of this section used is not
independent of the corrector, whose training target is the displacement between
a coarse Boris step and the same state carried by Boris at $h/150$.  Measured
against the closed form that reference carries $1.398\times10^{-3}$ Larmor radii of error of
its own, and the two error fields are anti-correlated at $\rho = -0.25$, so the
advantage it reports is $1.9$ per cent \emph{below} the true one rather than above
it: $117.8$ against $120.1$.  The closed form agrees with the independent DOP853
reference of Table~\ref{tab:family} to eleven significant figures.

%% --- ANCHOR C: replaces the 'trajectory advantage over Boris' row of
%% Table~\ref{tab:seeds} (line 1663).
    trajectory advantage over Boris            & $120.1$ & $143.1$ & $103.7$--$182.2$ & $8/20$ \\

%% --- ANCHOR D: a sentence for the caption of Table~\ref{tab:seeds}, replacing
%% 'that reference carries a trajectory error of $1.396\times10^{-3}$ ... above $298$'.
Both blocks are now scored against the closed form, so the two no longer differ
by their reference.  On the Boris reference at $h/150$ the same ensemble read
$152.8$ at the median with an upper quartile of $252.2$ and a maximum of $576.8$.  The
$3$ members whose reported error fell below that reference's own error of $1.397\times10^{-3}$
Larmor radii were exactly its $3$ largest advantages; on an independent ruler none
is below that floor and the maximum falls to $295.6$.
